q: 1. The type of pointing in which upper side of mortar joints is kept about 12 mm inside the face of the masonry and bottom is kept flushed with face of wall, is
explain: Struck pointing is designed to shed rainwater effectively. The slope created by recessing the top edge allows water to run off the joint rather than sitting on it.

q: 2. The portion of the wall between the facing and backing of the wall is called ...........
explain: The interior portion of a thick wall, situated between the external facing and internal backing, is filled with 'hearting' (usually rubble or lower-grade brick).

q: 3. The portion of the brick obtained by cutting into two portions longitudinally is called ...........
explain: A queen closer is a brick cut in half along its length. It is used to maintain the bond at the end of a wall (the quoin).

q: 4. The portion of the brick obtained by cutting it in transverse direction is called ...........
explain: A 'bat' is a piece of brick cut across its width. Common types include half-bats or three-quarter bats.

q: 5. The masonry with stone having chisel-dressed on all beds and joints to be true and square giving perfectly vertical & horizontal joint is called
explain: Ashlar masonry uses finely dressed stones with extremely thin joints, creating a very smooth and formal appearance compared to rubble masonry.

q: 6. The structure on which arch rests in called
explain: The abutment is the end support of an arch or bridge that resists the lateral thrust of the arch.

q: 7. The brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face of a wall, is known as
explain: A header is a brick laid so that its end (breadth) is visible on the face of the wall.

q: 8. A low height wall constructed along edge of the roof is called ...........
explain: A parapet wall is a low wall built at the edge of a roof or balcony for safety and to hide the roof surface.

q: 9. Which of the following wall is not designed for taking lateral load
explain: Gravity walls rely on their own weight to resist lateral earth pressure, but unlike buttress or counterfort walls, they aren't 'designed' with specific lateral reinforcement components.

q: 10. The cut or broken portion of brick is called
explain: A brick bat is a piece of brick with one or more ends cut off, usually across the width.

q: 11. The part of brick cut from a whole brick to maintain the bond in such a way that its one long face remains uncut is known as
explain: A closer is a portion of a brick used to close the bond at the end of a course, such as a queen closer or king closer.

q: 12. A projected stone in masonry wall provided to serve as a support to joist or truss is known as ...
explain: A corbel is a stone or brick projecting from a wall to support a heavy load, such as a beam, joist, or truss.

q: 13. The bond in which each course consists of alternate stretchers and headers is known as ..........
explain: In Flemish bond, headers and stretchers alternate within every single course, giving it a more decorative appearance than English bond.

q: 14. The English bond in which queen closers are placed next to quoin headers and a header is introduced next to the quoin stretcher in every alternate stretcher course ..........
explain: English cross bond is similar to English bond but staggers the stretcher courses by introducing an extra header at the quoin, creating a distinctive pattern.

q: 15. A bond in which a header course is provided only after few stretcher courses is known as ..........
explain: Garden wall bond is used for thin walls; it usually consists of one course of headers for every three or five courses of stretchers.

q: 16. A temporary structure erected with a purpose of providing a safe working platform is known as .......
explain: Scaffolding is the temporary framework used by workers to reach high sections of a building during construction or repair.

q: 17. Cavity walls ..........
options: prevent dampness from entering the building
have lesser dead load for given wall thickness
are better insulated against heat and sound
explain: The air gap in cavity walls prevents moisture transfer (dampness) and acts as an insulator for heat and noise.

q: 18. Spandril is ..........
options: the curved space formed between the extrados and the horizontal line through the crown
the space in the form of a sector between the intrados and the center of the arch
the curved space between the intrados and springing line
explain: A spandril is the triangular-like space between the outer curve (extrados) of an arch and a rectangular enclosure or horizontal line.

q: 19. If the center of the arch lies above the springing line, it is ..........
explain: In a horse-shoe arch, the curve continues past the semi-circle, meaning the center is above the line where it starts curving inward.

q: 20. An arch which is constructed either on a flat arch or on a wooden lintel to provide greater strength is called ..........
explain: A relieving arch is built above a lintel or flat arch to divert the weight of the wall above to the side supports.

q: 21. The vertical distance between the tops of two successive treads is called ..........
explain: Rise is the vertical height of a single step in a staircase.

q: 22. The material commonly used to cover the pitched roofs with steel trusses is ..........
options: thatched covering of reed or straw
explain: A.C. sheets (Asbestos Cement) or CGI sheets are the standard choice for covering industrial steel trusses due to their light weight and durability.

q: 23. Arches over openings are preferred to lintel beams when
options: loads are heavy and span is large
explain: Arches are superior to lintels for wide spans and heavy loads because they act in compression, provided strong supports are present.

q: 24. The angle of the skewback with the horizontal in the case of flat arches is usually
explain: For flat (camber) arches, the skewbacks are traditionally cut at a 60-degree angle.

q: 25. A projecting piece usually provided to support a truss, is
explain: A cornice is a decorative and functional horizontal projection at the top of a wall.

q: 26. While calculating the loads, the specific weight of brick masonry is generally taken as ..........
explain: The unit weight of standard common brick masonry is approximately 1920 kg/m³ (roughly 19 kN/m³).

q: 27. The wall constructed across the slope to protect the slope from the adverse effects is called ..........
explain: A breast wall is built to prevent the 'breasting' or sliding of natural earth slopes, whereas a retaining wall is designed to hold back artificial fills.

q: 28. For a building on the side of a busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on road, the type of scaffolding provided is ..........
explain: Needle scaffolding (cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' projecting from the wall, keeping the ground level clear for traffic.

q: 29. A course of stone provided immediately below a cornice, is called ..........
explain: In classical architecture and stone masonry, the frieze is the course located directly underneath the projecting cornice.

q: 30. A type of bond in which all the bricks are laid as headers on the faces of walls, is known as ..........
explain: Heading bond uses only headers and is useful for constructing curved walls or footings.

q: 31. In a raking bond ..........
options: the bricks are laid as headers
all the bricks are laid as stretchers
the arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond
the bonding bricks are laid at any angle other than zero or ninety degrees
explain: Raking bonds (like diagonal or herring-bone) involve laying bricks at an angle to increase longitudinal strength in thick walls.

q: 32. The total horizontal pressure (p) per meter length of retaining wall at a depth h meter is ..........
explain: According to Rankine's theory, the total active earth pressure is P = 1/2 * w * h² * Ka, where Ka = (1-sinΦ)/(1+sinΦ).

q: 33. A partition wall may be ..........
explain: Partition walls are non-load bearing internal walls used to divide space; they can be permanent (fixed) or movable (folding/collapsible).

q: 34. The inner surface of an arch is called ..........
explain: The intrados is the lower or inner curve of an arch.

q: 35. Herringbone bond is used for ..........
options: architectural finish to the face work
walls having thickness more than 4 bricks
explain: Herringbone bond is a decorative pattern where bricks are laid at 45 degrees, common in flooring and very thick walls.

q: 36. In which of the following arch, the center the arch is above the springing line?
explain: A Horse-shoe arch (Moorish arch) has a curve that continues beyond the semi-circle, putting the center above the springing line.

q: 37. Type of pointing in which V shaped projection is provided outside the wall surface is called ...........
explain: Toothed (or weathered) pointing involves creating a sloped or V-projection to help shed water from the joints.

q: 38. A pointed arch which forms equilateral or isosceles triangle is known as ...........
explain: A lancet arch is a narrow, sharply pointed arch characteristic of Gothic architecture.
